summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Cabezón earned his BS at Caltech and his PhD at UW-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) and UC Santa Barbara (2001).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Jotika Khur-Yearn earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Kramer studied under Lambert Schmithausen at Hamburg (PhD ~2004) and completed her habilitation at Munich. She taught at Munich (2017–2021) before becoming professor and institute head at Leipzig University in 2021.
Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Brennan completed a PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey.
Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under doctoral supervisor Max Deeg (attested 2012).

An Indologist and religious studies scholar, Törzsök completed a DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She served as associate professor at Lille 3 University (from 2001) and became professor (directeur d’études) at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2018.

A specialist in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Simmer-Brown completed a PhD at Walden University (~1978). In 1977, she joined Naropa University, where she became Distinguished Professor Emerita.

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Ahn earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. He served as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan (attested 2019).
Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Rhi completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.
Tanabe studied philosophy and other subjects, undertaking PhD studies at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and studying under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

A scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and joined the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques in 1839.

A linguist and Indologist, Bloch studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet, earning a doctorate from the University of Paris. He held chairs at the École des langues orientales (1921–1937) and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Levinson earned his PhD at the University of Virginia in 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins. He served as an assistant professor of religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

A historian educated at Lycée Charlemagne, Michelet served as maître de conférences at the École Normale Supérieure (from 1827), section chief at the Archives nationales (1831–1851), and professor of history at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology, Mohl studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy and Abel-Rémusat. He was an extraordinary professor at Tübingen (1826–1834) and Professor of Persian at the Collège de France (1847–1876).

A linguist and historian who earned his PhD at Kiel University, Oppert served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology at INALCO (from 1857) and professor of Assyriology at the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Specializing in Indology and architectural history, Hegewald completed a BA and PhD at SOAS, an MA at Oxford, and a habilitation at RWTH Aachen. In 2010, she became a professor at the University of Bonn.

A scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religion, Ching earned her doctorate from Australian National University (~1968–1971). After teaching at Columbia and Yale, she became a professor of religion, philosophy, and East Asian studies at the University of Toronto (1978).
A scholar of sinology and art history, Andrews studied at Brown, Harvard, and UC Berkeley. She joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.
Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Leslie held a post at SOAS University of London from approximately 1995 to 2004.
